title: Audit mapping scratchpad: micro-evidence experiments
content:
Purpose:

This is a messy scratchpad for small experiments and mapping heuristics for SOC2-style evidence collection. I want something lightweight we can trial with SRE/product before committing to the full inventory matrix. Not polished — notes to self and to whoever picks this up.

Background/context:
- We need an operational approach to collect, surface, and sanity-check evidence for logical access, change management, logging, and backups.
- Existing inventory is too large and brittle; engineering teams are burned by ad hoc requests. Goal: define mini-evidence artifacts that are quick to produce and verify ("micro-evidence") and iterate.

Hypothesis / approach:
1) For each control family, define 2–3 micro-evidence items that:
   - are cheap to generate (minutes–hours),
   - provide high signal for reviewers,
   - are scriptable or snapshot-able.
2) Automate capture where possible and place in a consistent evidence bucket with metadata (who ran it, timestamp, brief description).
3) For anything manual, require a one-paragraph narrative and a link to the artifact.

Candidate micro-evidence examples (sketch):
- IAM reviews: export of IAM role list filtered by service account tag + short mapping doc showing active principals and last-used time (CLI command output + grep / jq).
- Pipeline changes: CI job run log + PR link + small note stating whether reviewed via CODEOWNERS.
- Config drift: result of config-diff tool for critical infra (last 24h) showing 0 diffs or listing changes.
- Access logs: one-hour slice from s3 access logs (or CloudTrail) for the service account being assessed, plus a one-line summary of abnormal events.
- Backups: latest backup manifest (s3 key + size) + verify restore test result (manual small obj restore or snapshot).
- Alerting: screenshot of paging alert in OpsGenie/PagerDuty with timestamp + link to alert rule.

Mini-experiment plan (what to run this week):
- Pick 2 services: hosted-api and console (small scope).
- For each service, produce micro-evidence for: IAM reviews, pipeline changes, access logs slice, backup manifest.
- Timebox to 1 engineer-day per service.
- Store evidence in: s3://redwood-evidence/tmp/trust-2026/<service>/<artifact>-YYYYMMDD.json (or text).

Automation notes / commands (rough):
- IAM export: aws iam list-roles --query "Roles[?contains(AssumeRolePolicyDocument.Statement[].Principal.Service,'ec2.amazonaws.com')]=="  # placeholder
- CloudTrail slice: aws cloudtrail lookup-events --start-time 2026-03-08T10:00:00Z --end-time 2026-03-08T11:00:00Z --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=ResourceName,AttributeValue=<svc>
- Backup manifest: aws s3api list-objects --bucket redwood-backups --prefix <svc>/manifests/ --query 'Contents[0]'

Evidence metadata schema (minimal):
- generated_by (human/script), timestamp (UTC), service, artifact_type, link_to_blob, short_summary (1-2 sentences), run_command_or_pr

Open questions / blockers:
- Retention: how long do reviewers expect to keep these micro-records? 90 days? 365?
- Sensitive artifacts: do we need to redact PII or secrets before snapshot? (obvious, but tooling?).
- Ownership: who owns the evidence pipeline for each service? SRE or service team? (suggest SRE owns infra tooling, service team owns content correctness).
- Evidence auth/access: how to allow audit reviewers temporary read-only access without creating more tickets? Consider pre-signed URLs + short TTL.

Mapping thoughts (quick):
- Logical access controls -> IAM export + last-login summary + one page narrative.
- Change management -> PR + CI logs + CODEOWNERS signoff capture.
- Logging/monitoring -> log slice + alert screenshot + retention policy doc snippet.
- Backups -> manifest + restore smoke test + retention policy note.

Draft checklist for review run (for each service):
- [ ] generate IAM micro-export and store blob
- [ ] attach narrative (why these roles exist)
- [ ] produce one-hour log slice and short anomaly summary
- [ ] copy backup manifest and run small restore test
- [ ] collect recent PRs that changed infra config (last 30 days)
- [ ] drop artifacts into evidence bucket with metadata file
- [ ] ping trust-reviewer in Slack thread with presigned links

Notes from last run (2026-02-24 trial):
- Took ~4 hours per service to assemble everything manually (too slow). Biggest time sink: chasing PRs and reconstructing context.
- Pre-signed URL approach worked but we need automation to generate one-click reviewer links.
- For hosted-api, IAM export included dozens of stale roles — we should prioritize a stale-role clean-up sprint.

Potential follow-ups / next steps:
- Build a tiny CLI (python) that runs the micro-evidence checklist for a service and uploads artifacts to evidence bucket with metadata. Hook into internal tooling repo (see linked PR placeholder).
- Draft short-run playbook for reviewers: how to interpret micro-evidence, common red flags, quick accept/reject heuristics.
- Run one-week pilot with product+SRE and gather time-to-produce metrics.

Things to avoid in evidence blobs:
- Don't include stack traces containing secrets.
- Redact IP addresses when not necessary.
- Avoid long raw logs without a short summary; reviewers will ignore large blobs.

Questions for SRE (to drop into sync):
- Can we schedule a 30m sync to demo the pre-signed URL flow? (cc: Maya Chen)
- Do we already have a standard metadata format in infra-config? If yes, link it so micro-evidence aligns.
- Want SRE to own a script template that teams can run locally and upload.

Random brainstorms (quick):
- "Evidence receipts": when a micro-evidence artifact is produced, emit a JSON receipt and optionally email trust-reviewers. Could be useful for audit timelines.
- Lightweight attestation: service owners sign a 2-line attestation that they reviewed the artifacts and confirm no open issues. Store attestation as separate artifact.

TODO (short):
- [ ] Prototype CLI, attach to infra repo PR (#987 placeholder).
- [ ] Run pilot for hosted-api + console next week (assign: Riley).
- [ ] Draft reviewer playbook (1 pager) and store in Confluence TRUST-4492.

If you pick this up: sorry for the messy flow. Start with the checklist and aim to get one service to end-to-end micro-evidence in a day. Then we iterate.

-- Arjun
